See also: órbita, orbitá, òrbita, orbità, orbīta, orbītā, and orbită

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin orbita (“a circuit, orbit”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Received Pronunciation) IPA(key): /ˈɔː.bɪt.ə/
  • (General American) IPA(key): /ˈɔɹ.bət.ə/

Noun

[edit]

orbita (plural orbitae)

  1. (anatomy) Obsolete form of orbit.

Anagrams

[edit]
  • aborti, bioart

Indonesian

[edit]
Indonesian Wikipedia has an article on:
orbita
Wikipedia id

Etymology

[edit]

Learned borrowing from Latin orbita. Doublet of orbit.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Indonesian) IPA(key): /orˈbita/ [orˈbi.t̪a]
  • Rhymes: -ita
  • Syllabification: or‧bi‧ta

Noun

[edit]

orbita (plural orbita-orbita)

  1. orbit:
    1. (anatomy) the bony cavity in the skull of a vertebrate containing the eyeball
    2. (zoology) the area around the eye of a bird or other animal

Further reading

[edit]

Latin

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • orbita:
    • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ˈɔr.bɪ.ta]
    • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ˈɔr.bi.ta]
  • orbitā:
    • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ˈɔr.bɪ.taː]
    • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ˈɔr.bi.ta]

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Proto-Italic, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃erbʰ- (“to turn”), cognate to Umbrian 𐌖𐌓𐌚𐌄𐌕𐌀 (urfeta).

Two derivational pathways from that root include:[1]

  • Possibly from *orbes, orbitis ("going in a circle") +‎ -a, from orbis (“circle”) +‎ -es (“going”). Confer antistita, from antistes. This would imply Proto-Italic *orβitā.
  • Possibly a substantivization Proto-Italic *orβetā of a past participle *orβetos to an iterative verb *orβeō.

Compare typologically Russian колея́ (kolejá) (<< Proto-Indo-European *kʷelh₁-). Also compare кругове́рть (krugovértʹ) (akin to верте́ть (vertétʹ)).

Noun

[edit]

orbita f (genitive orbitae); first declension

  1. (literally, Classical Latin) A track or rut made in the ground by a wheel.
    1. (figurative, Old Latin, poetic) A path, track, course.
  2. An impression or mark left by a ligature.
  3. A circuit, orbit.
